ledger.claim: The deviation is established on this trip's own trace. EV-GPS-00701 records trace_distance_km of 26.85 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff events against a booked optimal of 20.7 km on EV-TRIP-00701, an excess of 6.15 km — 29.71% of optimal — so both POL-RD-01 tests pass: more than 20% of optimal AND more than 0.8 km absolute. POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure the governing one and forbids citing trip_record.actual_distance_km for the threshold test, so the finding rests on 26.85 km, and the excess is the excess remaining after every adjustment clause, none of which applies.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes, so the excess can be taken from it directly. EV-GPS-00701 carries 247 fixes at a 10 s cadence with coverage_pct 100.0, gaps [] and max_gap_sec 0.0, so none of POL-RD-07(a)'s >90 s gaps exists; the highest speed in the driver track's distinct_speeds_kph list is 46.4 km/h, which at a 10 s cadence cannot produce the >500 m consecutive-fix jump POL-RD-07(b) describes (that would need 180 km/h); and the sampling interval is 10 s, not the sustained >30 s interval in POL-RD-07(c). The claim therefore needs no independent corroboration and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation arises.

The rider has discharged the initial burden under POL-RD-08. Limb (a): the same trip identifier TRP-00701 runs through EV-TRIP-00701, EV-GPS-00701 and EV-FARE-00701, and the trace's first fix at 08:18:40 coincides with trip_record.started_at on the same date, so the artifacts describe the same trip. Limb (b): the excess above meets the POL-RD-01 threshold, measured from an unimpaired trace. The burden therefore shifts to the driver, who must point to a specific artifact and a specific clause under POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05, POL-RD-11 or POL-RD-12; the driver's statement points to none, and an assertion citing no evidence ID carries no weight.

The driver's explanation that 'she agreed to share' does not exonerate the detour under POL-RD-04. EV-CHAT-00701 contains exactly one message for this trip and it is the rider's own protest at 08:32:40 — 'I paid you 40 cash and you said no detour; why are we collecting someone?' — with waypoint_hint null and no road named. There is no rider instruction in the log at all, so POL-RD-04(a) to (c) cannot be satisfied, and because waypoint_hint is null the 200 m corroboration test is undecidable on the record: the clause is unavailable, the case is decided on the remaining clauses, and the ruling must record that the test could not be run.

No traffic advisory can excuse the excess, and I disclose the impairment of the artifact I cite for that: EV-ADVIS-00701-01 is MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and I cite it because the absence itself is citable under POL-GEN-02. POL-RD-03 requires an advisory naming a road or segment the optimal route traverses, with a validity window overlapping the time the trace shows the vehicle would have reached it, matched by a trace that leaves the corridor before that segment and rejoins after; no such advisory exists in this bundle, so the comparison cannot be run and the driver cannot invoke POL-RD-03. To the extent any external traffic cause is relied on at the hearing, POL-RD-13 confines the test to this trip's advisory and a missing advisory carries no weight.

Collecting a second passenger buys the driver nothing under POL-RD-12, because that clause applies only where trip_record.vehicle_type is RYDE_POOL. EV-TRIP-00701 shows vehicle_type RYDE_X and solo_optimal_distance_km null, so there is no platform-matched itinerary and no matched-itinerary baseline: the only numeric baseline is the booked 20.7 km optimal, and distance added to collect another passenger is not excluded from the POL-RD-01 excess. The driver's own account of a share arrangement, and the rider's contemporaneous message asking why someone was being collected (EV-CHAT-00701), place the vehicle off the booked itinerary of a non-pooled booking.

I do not overstate the money on this side of the case, and the record is clear against a distance refund. Because EV-FARE-00701 shows fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd 27.40, POL-RD-11 closes the distance-and-time route: the rider's only remedy is the amount by which charged_total exceeds quoted_fare_sgd plus the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09, and that is 27.40 less 27.40 less 0.00 = 0.00, exactly the ledger's own pol_rd_11_remedy of 0.00. There is no ERP line (erp_gantries is empty, tolls_erp 0.0) and no airport surcharge (airport_surcharge 0.00; the trip ends at, and does not originate at, an airport), so no POL-RD-09 pass-through correction is available either. The SGD 40 the rider says was handed over in cash appears nowhere on the platform ledger and no clause of this policy reaches off-platform money: the request to refund the entire platform fare cannot be granted on this record, and what the record supports is the deviation finding itself.

The rider claims no uplift she is not entitled to. The excess of 6.15 km and 29.71% is below both materiality limbs of POL-RD-01 (50% of optimal, and 8.0 km absolute), so POL-RD-06 is not engaged by materiality; and on the two fields POL-RD-06 does name, driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 250, a ratio of 0.00, far below the 0.05 pattern threshold with the 40-trip minimum satisfied. No pattern is therefore established on this record and no POL-RD-06(b) uplift or POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral follows.

This trip was sold on an UPFRONT_QUOTE: the quoted fare of SGD 27.40 on the fare breakdown is exactly the SGD 27.40 total charged, so the rider paid the price she accepted at booking and there is no overcharge for a refund to reach.

Under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges on an upfront-quoted trip were fixed at booking, so the rider was never out of pocket on those lines however far the vehicle drove; POL-RD-02 does not run and no distance-or-time refund is available, whether the trace excess is taken at 6.15 km or at any other figure.

Every pass-through and statutory line on the ledger is zero — no ERP gantries charged (tolls_erp 0.00), airport surcharge 0.00, waiting-time fee 0.00 — so the amount by which charged_total exceeds quoted_fare_sgd plus the properly chargeable lines under POL-RD-11(a) is SGD 0.00, and the fare computation itself records a POL-RD-11 remedy of 0.00.

There is no off-route or phantom charge for POL-RD-09(4) to correct: the fare breakdown carries no ERP gantry entries at all (erp_gantries empty) and the airport surcharge line is 0.00, consistent with a trip that ends at an airport rather than originating at one.

The trace shows an excess of 6.15 km, 29.71% of the 20.7 km optimal — above the POL-RD-01 establishment gate but below the material gate (neither greater than 50% nor greater than 8.0 km) — so no POL-RD-06 repeat-pattern check is engaged; and in any event driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 250 completed_trips_90d, far below both the 3-flag and the 5% pattern thresholds, so no pattern exists and no conduct uplift follows.

The SGD 40 cash the rider says she handed over appears nowhere on the fare breakdown and is not a platform charge; the SGD 27.40 contested is the platform fare alone, and POL-RD-11 confines the rider's remedies to the lines of the fare breakdown, so an off-ledger cash allegation the driver denies cannot ground a platform refund.

The driver's trace is complete and unimpaired for policy purposes: 247 fixes at a 10 s cadence, coverage_pct 100.0, max_gap_sec 0.0 and no gaps at all, so POL-RD-07(a) to (c) is not triggered and the measured excess stands on a clean, unimpaired trace.

None of POL-RD-10's escalation triggers fires: the trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; the trace is gap-free and unimpaired; the timestamps run forward consistently (requested 08:12, started 08:18:40, ended 08:59:40); and the computed refund is 0.00, far below the SGD 150 ceiling — so a monetary ruling is available and the disputed amount need not be held for a human reviewer.

NO_ACTION under POL-GEN-03 is party-relative and leaves fare_breakdown.payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 exactly as they stand; on this rider-filed dispute that preserves the upfront fare the driver earned under the booking quote, rather than reversing it.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider: your fare was an upfront quote and it was charged exactly as quoted, so no platform refund is due on it. EV-FARE-00701 shows fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE, quoted_fare_sgd 27.40 and total_charged 27.40, with charged_over_quote 0.00. The trip did deviate - EV-GPS-00701 measures 26.85 km driven against a booked optimal of 20.7 km on EV-TRIP-00701, an excess of 6.15 km (29.71% of optimal), over the POL-RD-01 gate of 20% and 0.8 km - but on an upfront-quoted fare POL-RD-11 fixes the distance and time charges at booking, so a detour costs you nothing on those lines and POL-RD-02 does not run. Your only remedy is the amount by which the charge exceeded the quote plus properly chargeable pass-through lines: 27.40 less 27.40 less 0.00 = 0.00, which is the ledger's own pol_rd_11_remedy of 0.00. There are no ERP gantries (erp_gantries empty, tolls 0.00), no airport surcharge (0.00 - the trip ends at an airport, it does not originate at one) and no waiting-time fee, so no POL-RD-09 pass-through correction is available either. The SGD 40 cash you say you handed over does not appear anywhere on the platform ledger and no clause of this policy reaches off-platform money; nothing is decided on that head. To the driver: your account that she agreed to share does not excuse the detour. POL-RD-04 needs a rider instruction recorded in the chat log; the only message for this trip (EV-CHAT-00701) is the rider's own protest asking why another passenger was being collected, its waypoint_hint is null and no road is named, so the 200 m corroboration test could not be run and POL-RD-04 is unavailable. The vehicle was RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline does not apply. No fine follows, however, because the upfront fare already puts the distance-and-time economics on your side. The deviation is established but not material: 6.15 km and 29.71% are below both material limbs (8.0 km and 50% of optimal), so POL-RD-06 is not engaged by materiality; on its named fields driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 250 completed_trips_90d (ratio 0.00, below the 0.05 threshold), so no repeat pattern exists and no conduct referral follows. The trace is unimpaired for POL-RD-07 purposes (247 fixes at a 10 s cadence, coverage 100%, max_gap_sec 0.0, no gaps), so no independent corroboration is needed and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation arises; no other POL-RD-10 trigger fires either - trip identifiers and timestamps match and the computed refund is 0.00. The missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00701-01, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) is cited by no one to excuse the route, so POL-RD-03 is simply unavailable and POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged. Ruling: NO_ACTION. The fare breakdown's payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 stand as they are.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
